claim: 53BP1 is a 200 kDa protein involved in DNA repair and cell cycle regulation.
source: Anti-tumor protein p53 binding protein (53BP1) is a 200 kDa protein involved in DNA repair and cell cycle regulation (Iwabuchi et al., 1994; Rappold et al., 2001; Mirza-Aghazadeh-Attari et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work establishing 53BP1's molecular weight and functions.

claim: BRCA1 and 53BP1 together regulate pathway selection for DNA double-strand break repair.
source: Together, breast cancer type 1 susceptibility gene (BRCA1) and 53BP1 regulate pathway selection for DNA double-strand break repair (Gupta et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 53BP1 binds and protects DNA ends formed by double-strand breaks, limiting end resection and promoting use of nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) for DNA repair.
source: 53BP1 binds and protects DNA ends formed by double-strand breaks, limiting end resection and promoting use of nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) for DNA repair (Rappold et al., 2001; Ward et al., 2003; Becker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: BRCA1 is necessary for the eviction of 53BP1 from chromatin, allowing for end resection factors to initiate homology-directed repair (HDR).
source: BRCA1 is necessary for the eviction of 53BP1 from chromatin, allowing for end resection factors to initiate homology-directed repair (HDR) (Bouwman et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: In the absence of functional BRCA1, the HDR pathway is nonfunctional, and error-prone NHEJ dominates double-strand break repair.
source: In the absence of functional BRCA1, the HDR pathway is nonfunctional, and error-prone NHEJ dominates double-strand break repair (Bunting et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Aberrant NHEJ results in genome instability such as chromosomal rearrangements and radial chromosome formation.
source: Aberrant NHEJ results in genome instability such as chromosomal rearrangements and radial chromosome formation.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of NHEJ consequences.

claim: Chemotherapy drugs such as PARPi and platinum-based drugs are effective against BRCA-negative cancers.
source: Chemotherapy drugs such as PARPi and platinum-based drugs are effective against BRCA-negative cancers (Rappold et al., 2001; Becker et al., 2018; Al-Ejeh et al., 2010; West et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In BRCA-negative cells, inactivation of 53BP1 once again activates HDR, resulting in loss of efficacy of PARPi and other chemotherapy agents.
source: However, in BRCA-negative cells, inactivation of 53BP1 once again activates HDR, resulting in loss of efficacy of PARPi and other chemotherapy agents.
evidence: Based on logical inference from the relationship between 53BP1, HDR, and chemotherapy efficacy.

claim: In response to DNA damage, 53BP1 forms nuclear bodies which mark sites of DNA double-strand breaks.
source: In response to DNA damage, 53BP1 forms nuclear bodies which mark sites of DNA double-strand breaks (Becker et al., 2018; Schultz et al., 2000; Kilic et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Upon induction of DNA damage, 53BP1 is recruited to sites of DNA double-strand break and is retained on chromatin through interactions between modified histones and the tudor domain, ubiquitin-dependent recognition domain, and oligomerization domain.
source: Upon induction of DNA damage, 53BP1 is recruited to sites of DNA double-strand break and is retained on chromatin through interactions between modified histones and the tudor domain (Zgheib et al., 2009), ubiquitin-dependent recognition domain (Fradet-Turcotte et al., 2013), and oligomerization domain (OD) (Kelliher et al., 2024; Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The long N-terminal disordered domain of 53BP1 (residues 1–1230) contains 28 putative ATM kinase recognition (S/TQ) motifs.
source: The long N-terminal disordered domain of 53BP1 (residues 1–1230), which contains 28 putative ATM kinase recognition (S/TQ) motifs, is phosphorylated by ATM kinase at multiple sites (Zgheib et al., 2005; Jowsey et al., 2007)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The N-terminal disordered domain of 53BP1 is phosphorylated by ATM kinase at multiple sites.
source: The long N-terminal disordered domain of 53BP1 (residues 1–1230), which contains 28 putative ATM kinase recognition (S/TQ) motifs, is phosphorylated by ATM kinase at multiple sites (Zgheib et al., 2005; Jowsey et al., 2007)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Phosphorylation of 53BP1 by ATM kinase results in recruitment of downstream effectors active in protection of DNA ends (e.g. RIF1, Rev7, and Shieldin) or in NHEJ (e.g. PTIP).
source: which results in recruitment of downstream effectors active in protection of DNA ends (e.g. RIF1 [Zimmermann et al., 2013], Rev7 [Ghezraoui et al., 2018], and Shieldin [Noordermeer et al., 2018]) or in NHEJ (e.g. PTIP [Wu et al., 2009]).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: 53BP1 contains 3 LC8 recognition motifs at the C-terminus of its disordered domain (residues 1150–1230).
source: 53BP1 contains 3 LC8 recognition motifs at the C-terminus of its disordered domain (residues 1150–1230) (Lo et al., 2005; Howe et al., 2022)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The oligomerization domain of 53BP1 spans residues 1231–1272.
source: followed by the OD (Zgheib et al., 2009) (residues 1231–1272), which is poorly characterized.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: LC8 is a hub protein that binds >100 client proteins at their disordered regions in its two symmetric binding grooves, facilitating the dimerization of the client proteins.
source: LC8 is a hub protein that binds >100 client proteins at their disordered regions in its two symmetric binding grooves, facilitating the dimerization of the client proteins (Jespersen et al., 2019a; Benison et al., 2007; Barbar and Nyarko, 2015; Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Either the OD mutant (ODm) or LC8 binding mutant (LC8m) reduces 53BP1 nuclear bodies.
source: Either the OD mutant (ODm) or LC8 binding mutant (LC8m) reduces 53BP1 nuclear bodies, and a construct containing both mutations reduces nuclear bodies to levels similar to the control (Becker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A construct containing both OD and LC8 binding mutations reduces 53BP1 nuclear bodies to levels similar to the control.
source: Either the OD mutant (ODm) or LC8 binding mutant (LC8m) reduces 53BP1 nuclear bodies, and a construct containing both mutations reduces nuclear bodies to levels similar to the control (Becker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The LC8 binding mutant shows reduced DNA repair activity.
source: Furthermore, the LC8m shows reduced DNA repair activity, while the ODm is inactive in DNA repair, and the LC8m/ODm construct is not even efficiently recruited to nuclear bodies.
evidence: Based on inference from the manuscript's discussion of mutant phenotypes.

claim: The OD mutant is inactive in DNA repair.
source: Furthermore, the LC8m shows reduced DNA repair activity, while the ODm is inactive in DNA repair, and the LC8m/ODm construct is not even efficiently recruited to nuclear bodies.
evidence: Based on inference from the manuscript's discussion of mutant phenotypes.

claim: The LC8m/ODm construct is not efficiently recruited to nuclear bodies.
source: Furthermore, the LC8m shows reduced DNA repair activity, while the ODm is inactive in DNA repair, and the LC8m/ODm construct is not even efficiently recruited to nuclear bodies.
evidence: Based on inference from the manuscript's discussion of mutant phenotypes.

claim: LC8 binds a highly variable short linear recognition motif in disordered regions of client proteins.
source: LC8 binds a highly variable short linear recognition motif in disordered regions of client proteins (Figure 1C; Jespersen et al., 2019a; Benison et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: A well-conserved triad, TQT, most frequently occupies the anchor of the LC8 binding motif.
source: A well-conserved triad, TQT, most frequently occupies the anchor of this motif, but the entire sequence is variable.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of LC8 binding motifs.

claim: 53BP1 OD is a homogeneous trimer.
source: Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) of the OD (1200–1290) shows a mass of 39.2±0.6 kDa as an average of 4 runs loaded at concentrations between 75 and 750 μM (dilution over column is ~10×) (Figure 1F), which suggests a trimeric form dominates in this concentration range (expected trimer mass of 39.5 kDa) and that the OD is a stable trimer.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data showing mass consistent with trimer across concentration range.

claim: LBD-OD is a trimer.
source: LBD-OD shows a single peak with a mass of 50 kDa (Figure 1H). Since the calculated mass expected for a monomeric LBD-OD is 17.0 kDa, the mass measured by SEC-MALS suggests that LBD-OD is a trimer (expected mass of 51 kDa for trimer).
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data showing mass consistent with trimer.

claim: 53BP1 is the first trimeric client of LC8.
source: To date, all known oligomeric clients of LC8 are either dimers or tetramers, and thus the mechanism for complex formation between a dimer and a trimer is not known.
evidence: Based on comparison to established knowledge of LC8 clients.

claim: The OD of 53BP1 contains primarily beta-sheet structure with some propensity for alpha-helical structure.
source: Circular dichroism (CD) of a construct of the OD spanning residues 1200–1290 shows a single minimum near 218 nm (Figure 1D) consistent with a primarily beta-sheet structure. Fitting this data with BeStSel (Micsonai et al., 2015) estimates a primarily beta-sheet structure with some propensity for an alpha-helical structure (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data and BeStSel analysis.

claim: The LBD remains disordered in the context of the OD.
source: The LBD remains disordered in the context of the OD, as shown by a sharp peak near 200 nm and a smaller minimum around 218 nm in the CD spectrum, consistent with a primarily disordered structure containing some beta-sheet structure (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by CD spectroscopy data.

claim: The ordered domain of LBD-OD is between residues 1225 and 1290.
source: The spectrum of LBD alone (residues 1140–1225) contains only the minimum at 200 nm, indicating the ordered domain of LBD-OD is between residues 1225 and 1290 (Figure 1G; Zgheib et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by comparison of CD spectra of LBD and LBD-OD, and citation to prior work.

claim: Both LBD-OD and OD have a Tm at 57°C.
source: Both LBD-OD (Figure 1G) and OD (data not shown) have a Tm at 57°C.
evidence: Supported by thermal denaturation data.

claim: LBD-OD and OD refold reversibly.
source: Refolding curves show no hysteresis, indicating that both LBD-OD and OD refold reversibly.
evidence: Supported by thermal denaturation/refolding data.

claim: Most residues of the LBD in the context of the OD show similar dynamic behavior to that of the LBD alone.
source: Most residues of the LBD in the context of the OD show similar dynamic behavior to that of the LBD alone, indicating that the LBD remains disordered in the LBD-OD construct (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: Supported by NMR relaxation data (R1, R2, NOE).

claim: Residues 1210–1225 appear less dynamic with high R2 values compared to those for the same residues in the LBD alone.
source: However, residues 1210–1225, which are at the end of the LBD, appear less dynamic with high R2 values (Figure 2C) compared to those for the same residues in the LBD alone, as expected due to its proximity to a self-associated domain.
evidence: Supported by NMR R2 relaxation data.

claim: Titration of LBD-OD with LC8 shows uniform signal attenuation for residues 1150–1200, suggesting no binding preference for any particular site.
source: Titration of LBD-OD with LC8 shows similar uniform signal attenuation for the same residues (Figure 2F), suggesting that the cooperative binding of LBD is conserved in the presence of the OD.
evidence: Supported by NMR titration data.

claim: LBD-OD with excess LC8 forms a heterogeneous complex containing at least three major populations with masses in the 120–296 kDa range.
source: SEC-MALS of LBD-OD with excess LC8 shows a heterogeneous complex containing at least three major populations (Figure 3B) with masses in the 120–296 kDa range (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: A complex containing 1 LBD-OD trimer and 3 LC8 dimers has an expected mass of 114 kDa.
source: A complex containing 1 LBD-OD trimer and 3 LC8 dimers is expected to have a mass of 114 kDa, and a complex containing 2 LBD-OD trimers and 9 LC8 dimers would have a mass of 293 KDa (Table 2), which are both consistent with the measured masses.
evidence: Based on calculation from known molecular weights.

claim: A complex containing 2 LBD-OD trimers and 9 LC8 dimers has an expected mass of 293 kDa.
source: A complex containing 1 LBD-OD trimer and 3 LC8 dimers is expected to have a mass of 114 kDa, and a complex containing 2 LBD-OD trimers and 9 LC8 dimers would have a mass of 293 KDa (Table 2), which are both consistent with the measured masses.
evidence: Based on calculation from known molecular weights.

claim: LBD-OD forms a trimeric complex with 3 dimers of LC8 and a bridged complex containing 2 trimers of LBD-OD and up to 9 dimers of LC8.
source: Our SEC-MALS suggests that LBD-OD forms a trimeric complex with 3 dimers of LC8 and a bridged complex containing 2 trimers of LBD-OD and up to 9 dimers of LC8 (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data and inference from mass measurements.

claim: QT2-OD retains a small fraction of a larger presumably bridged complex upon dilution during SEC.
source: QT3-OD is exclusively a single complex, while QT2-OD retains a small fraction of a larger presumably bridged complex.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: QT2 is necessary to form stable intermolecular interactions resulting in intact bridged complexes.
source: Analysis of the two-site QT variants further demonstrated that complexes containing intact QT2 have populations with larger masses consistent with the bridged complex. These findings suggest that QT2 is necessary to form stable intermolecular interactions resulting in intact bridged complexes.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS and SV-AUC data showing only QT2-containing constructs maintain bridged complexes.

claim: QT2 is the only site with an unfavorable entropy in LC8 binding.
source: Importantly, QT2 is the only site with an unfavorable entropy, and QT1 is the weakest binding site overall.
evidence: Supported by ITC data from prior work (Howe et al., 2022).

claim: QT1 is the weakest binding site overall in 53BP1-LC8 interactions.
source: Importantly, QT2 is the only site with an unfavorable entropy, and QT1 is the weakest binding site overall.
evidence: Supported by ITC data from prior work (Howe et al., 2022).

claim: Wild-type LBD-OD shows a stoichiometry near 3:1 (3 LC8:1 53BP1) in ITC experiments.
source: The wild-type (WT) LBD-OD (Figure 5A) shows a stoichiometry near 3:1 (3 LC8:1 53BP1; or 3 LC8 dimers and 1 trimer of 53BP1; or 9 LC8 dimers and 2 trimers of 53BP1).
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: QT2 is the only one-site mutant with unfavorable entropy in LC8 binding.
source: The one-site LBD-ODm (Figure 5B–E) have similar binding properties to LBD (Howe et al., 2022) in that QT2 is the only one-site mutant with unfavorable entropy.
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: QT2-OD has the smallest difference in affinity between intratrimer and bridging interactions.
source: The variant with the smallest difference between bridging affinity and intratrimer interactions is QT2-OD (intratrimer Kd = 0.3 µM, intertrimer Kd = 1.1 µM).
evidence: Supported by ITC data analyzed with subsequent binding sites model.

claim: QT2 binding may pay the entropic penalty for bridging 53BP1 trimers.
source: Since all LBD-ODm containing QT2 have sigmoidal isotherms, we attribute the non-sigmoidal isotherms to the formation of a trimeric intermediate and suggest that QT2 binding may pay the entropic penalty for bridging 53BP1 trimers.
evidence: Based on inference from ITC isotherm shapes and thermodynamic analysis.

claim: Shortening the linker between LBD and OD by 5 residues results in a population shift to a larger presumably bridged complex.
source: Shortening the linker by 5 residues results in a population shift to a larger presumably bridged complex, and further reducing the length by 15 residues shifts the population to an almost completely larger bridged complex (Figure 6B), suggesting that shortening the LBD-OD linker stabilizes the dimer-of-trimers complex (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data of linker deletion mutants.

claim: Further reducing the linker length by 15 residues shifts the population to an almost completely larger bridged complex.
source: Shortening the linker by 5 residues results in a population shift to a larger presumably bridged complex, and further reducing the length by 15 residues shifts the population to an almost completely larger bridged complex (Figure 6B), suggesting that shortening the LBD-OD linker stabilizes the dimer-of-trimers complex (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data of linker deletion mutants.

claim: The entropic contribution becomes more favorable as the linker length is decreased.
source: The entropic contribution becomes more favorable as the linker length is decreased, while the overall affinity of the interaction is unchanged (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by ITC data of linker deletion mutants.

claim: The overall affinity of the LC8-53BP1 interaction is unchanged by linker length reduction.
source: The entropic contribution becomes more favorable as the linker length is decreased, while the overall affinity of the interaction is unchanged (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by ITC data of linker deletion mutants.

claim: The phosphomimetic T1171E elutes completely as a trimer complex, like QT13-OD.
source: As expected, T1171E elutes completely as a trimer complex, like QT13-OD, while both T117I and T1171V form a mixture of complexes, presumably a trimer and bridged complexes.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: T1171I forms a similar population of trimer and bridged complex to the wild-type.
source: T1171I forms a similar population of trimer and bridged complex to the WT, while T1171V forms a significantly higher population of the larger bridged complex (Figure 7B)
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: T1171V forms a significantly higher population of the larger bridged complex compared to wild-type.
source: T1171I forms a similar population of trimer and bridged complex to the WT, while T1171V forms a significantly higher population of the larger bridged complex (Figure 7B)
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: Sequence specificity of QT2 is a major determinant of 53BP1 heterogeneity.
source: indicating that sequence specificity of QT2 is a major determinant of 53BP1 heterogeneity.
evidence: Based on inference from SEC-MALS data of QT2 sequence variants.

claim: The anchor of QT2 is well conserved in animals.
source: BLAST analysis of the human 53BP1 sequence shows that the anchor of QT2 is well conserved in animals, in support of a critical role for 53BP1-LC8 interactions being tuned to maintain heterogeneity of 53BP1 oligomerization.
evidence: Supported by BLAST sequence analysis.

claim: The phosphodeficient mutant T1171I produces an enhancement in 53BP1 foci similar to the wild-type protein.
source: The phosphodeficient mutant (T1171I) produces an enhancement in 53BP1 foci similar to the WT protein (79 ± 7% for T1171I vs 85 ± 3% for WT)
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments.

claim: The phosphomimetic T1171E shows no significant difference in the number of cells with >10 foci over a mutant with all three QTs mutated.
source: while the phosphomimetic shows no significant difference in the number of cells with >10 foci over a mutant with all three QTs mutated (47 ± 12% for T1171E vs 47 ± 5% for LC8 binding null) (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments.

claim: QT2 is not phosphorylated in response to ionizing radiation.
source: The similarity of the phosphodeficient mutant to the WT and the strong loss of foci in the phosphomimetic show that QT2 is not phosphorylated in response to ionizing radiation and argues against the importance of phosphorylation at this site in nuclear repair foci.
evidence: Based on inference from comparison of phosphodeficient and phosphomimetic mutant phenotypes.

claim: Constructs with QT2 binding removed by AAA mutation fail to show a significant improvement in focus formation over the LC8 binding null mutant.
source: Constructs with QT2 binding removed by AAA mutation (QT3 and QT13) fail to show a significant improvement in focus formation over the LC8 binding null mutant, while the mutant containing only QT2 does provide an enhancement.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments.

claim: The mutant containing only QT2 provides an enhancement in 53BP1 focus formation.
source: Constructs with QT2 binding removed by AAA mutation (QT3 and QT13) fail to show a significant improvement in focus formation over the LC8 binding null mutant, while the mutant containing only QT2 does provide an enhancement.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from cell culture experiments.

claim: QT2 plays a role in regulating the enhancement from LC8 in focus formation of 53BP1.
source: All of this together suggest a role for QT2 in regulating the enhancement from LC8 in focus formation of 53BP1, which we propose to be mediated through heterogeneous bridging of 53BP1 trimers.
evidence: Based on inference from cell culture data and in vitro biophysical data.

claim: The primary role of LC8 is to bridge 53BP1 trimers, which in turn promotes recruitment of 53BP1 at sites of DNA damage.
source: 53BP1 mutants deficient in bridged species fail to impact 53BP1 focus formation in human cell culture studies, suggesting that the primary role of LC8 is to bridge 53BP1 trimers, which in turn promotes recruitment of 53BP1 at sites of DNA damage.
evidence: Based on inference from combined in vitro and cell culture data.

claim: The formation of higher-order oligomers of 53BP1 explains how LC8 elicits an improvement in 53BP1 foci.
source: We propose that the formation of higher-order oligomers of 53BP1 explains how LC8 elicits an improvement in 53BP1 foci and affects the structure and functions of 53BP1.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined data.

claim: LC8 binding is not required for 53BP1 focus formation.
source: While LC8 binding is not required for focus formation (Kilic et al., 2019), it improves focus formation and recruitment of 53BP1 to chromatin (Becker et al., 2018; West et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: LC8 binding improves focus formation and recruitment of 53BP1 to chromatin.
source: While LC8 binding is not required for focus formation (Kilic et al., 2019), it improves focus formation and recruitment of 53BP1 to chromatin (Becker et al., 2018; West et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: 53BP1 is the first trimeric client of LC8 reported.
source: While clients of LC8 are often dimers (Barbar and Nyarko, 2014; Gaik et al., 2015; Jespersen et al., 2019b), and occasionally tetramers (Szaniszló et al., 2022; Rodriguez Galvan et al., 2021), there are no reports of trimeric clients. Interestingly, we find that 53BP1 is a trimer
evidence: Inferred from statement that there are no prior reports of trimeric LC8 clients and the finding that 53BP1 is trimeric.

claim: The dimer-of-trimers complex can bind up to three histones bivalently, resulting in high avidity and retention in DNA repair foci.
source: Both the trimer and bridged complexes can bind multiple histones, but the dimer-of-trimers could bind up to three histones (blue) bivalently, resulting in high avidity and retention in DNA repair foci (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural data.

claim: Heterogeneity in 53BP1-LC8 complexes may allow for improved recruitment of 53BP1 into nuclear repair foci.
source: We speculate that heterogeneity in 53BP1-LC8 complexes may allow for improved recruitment of 53BP1 into nuclear repair foci, and the bridged complex stabilizes interactions with chromatin by allowing for more bivalent interactions (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: The bridged complex stabilizes interactions with chromatin by allowing for more bivalent interactions.
source: We speculate that heterogeneity in 53BP1-LC8 complexes may allow for improved recruitment of 53BP1 into nuclear repair foci, and the bridged complex stabilizes interactions with chromatin by allowing for more bivalent interactions (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: The OD of 53BP1 spans residues 1231–1279 based on truncation studies.
source: The OD of 53BP1 spans residues 1231–1279 based on truncation studies (Zgheib et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Disorder prediction by IUPred suggests that residues 1240–1270 are ordered.
source: Disorder prediction by IUPred (Erdős et al., 2021) suggests that residues 1240–1270 are ordered.
evidence: Based on computational prediction using IUPred.

claim: Neither Waggawagga nor Marcoil predicts any coiled-coils in the OD region of 53BP1.
source: Neither Waggawagga (Kollmar and Simm, 2019) nor Marcoil (Delorenzi and Speed, 2002) predicts any coiled-coils in this region.
evidence: Based on computational predictions using coiled-coil prediction tools.

claim: AlphaFold2 and PsiPred predict an entirely beta-sheet structure for the 53BP1 OD.
source: AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021) and PsiPred (McGuffin et al., 2000) predict an entirely beta-sheet structure, while JPred (Drozdetskiy et al., 2015) predicts a mixture of alpha-helices and beta-strands.
evidence: Based on computational structure predictions.

claim: JPred predicts a mixture of alpha-helices and beta-strands for the 53BP1 OD.
source: AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021) and PsiPred (McGuffin et al., 2000) predict an entirely beta-sheet structure, while JPred (Drozdetskiy et al., 2015) predicts a mixture of alpha-helices and beta-strands.
evidence: Based on computational structure predictions.

claim: The increased structure in 53BP1 OD is due to some folding upon oligomerization.
source: Since the BeStSel CD-based structure analysis estimates a higher percentage of structure than the sequence-based predictions, we conclude that the increased structure is due to some folding upon oligomerization (Figure 1E).
evidence: Based on inference from comparison of CD-based and sequence-based structure predictions.

claim: The 1H-15N HSQC of LBD-OD shows low peak dispersion and overlays well with the HSQC of LBD.
source: The 1H-15N heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) of LBD-OD shows low peak dispersion and overlays well with the HSQC of LBD (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by NMR HSQC data.

claim: No additional peaks for the OD were detected in the concentration range of 50–400 μM and in the temperature range of 10–40°C.
source: No additional peaks for the OD were detected in the concentration range of 50–400 μM and in the temperature range of 10–40°C.
evidence: Supported by NMR HSQC data.

claim: Cα-Cβ chemical shift indexing of LBD and LBD-OD shows shifts less than 0.5 for most residues, indicating that both constructs are disordered between residues 1140 and 1225.
source: Cα-Cβ chemical shift indexing of LBD and LBD-OD shows shifts less than 0.5 for most residues, indicating that both constructs are disordered between residues 1140 and 1225 (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by NMR chemical shift indexing data.

claim: The cooperative binding of LBD to LC8 is conserved in the presence of the OD.
source: Titration of LBD-OD with LC8 shows similar uniform signal attenuation for the same residues (Figure 2F), suggesting that the cooperative binding of LBD is conserved in the presence of the OD.
evidence: Based on inference from NMR titration data.

claim: Dimeric LBD-OD with 3 LC8 dimers has a calculated mass of 95 kDa.
source: Dimeric LBD-OD with 3 LC8 dimers has a calculated mass of 95 kDa, much smaller than what we observed.
evidence: Based on calculation from known molecular weights.

claim: QT2-OD shows two peaks in SV-AUC, indicating a mixture of different size complexes.
source: In sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV-AUC) of one-site LBD-ODm (Figure 4B), two peaks were observed for QT2-OD, indicating a mixture of different size complexes
evidence: Supported by SV-AUC data.

claim: QT3-OD primarily forms a single larger complex in SV-AUC.
source: while QT3-OD primarily formed a single larger complex.
evidence: Supported by SV-AUC data.

claim: All two-site QT variants show multiple complexes in excess LC8 by SV-AUC.
source: All the two-site QT variants (Figure 4B) show multiple complexes in excess LC8 supporting the presence of an activation barrier between the different size complexes, which differs depending on the QT variants used.
evidence: Supported by SV-AUC data.

claim: There is an activation barrier between the different size complexes of 53BP1-LC8, which differs depending on the QT variants used.
source: All the two-site QT variants (Figure 4B) show multiple complexes in excess LC8 supporting the presence of an activation barrier between the different size complexes, which differs depending on the QT variants used.
evidence: Based on inference from SV-AUC data showing multiple species.

claim: QT3-OD is exclusively a single complex in SEC-MALS.
source: In contrast to SV-AUC, QT3-OD is exclusively a single complex, while QT2-OD retains a small fraction of a larger presumably bridged complex.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: QT1-OD is fully dissociated in SEC-MALS.
source: QT1-OD is fully dissociated, and so we do not include it in our analysis.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: While both QT2 and QT3 mutants can form bridged complexes with excess LC8 as observed by SV-AUC, only QT2-OD maintains stable bridging upon dilution during SEC.
source: This difference between SEC and SV-AUC profiles suggests that while both QT2 and QT3 mutants can form bridged complexes with excess LC8 as observed by SV-AUC, only QT2-OD maintains stable bridging upon dilution during SEC.
evidence: Based on inference from comparison of SV-AUC and SEC-MALS data.

claim: Complexes containing intact QT2 have populations with larger masses consistent with the bridged complex.
source: Analysis of the two-site QT variants further demonstrated that complexes containing intact QT2 have populations with larger masses consistent with the bridged complex.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: LC8 binding to LBD-OD and the one- and two-site mutants shows enthalpically favorable interactions with Kd in the sub-micromolar to low micromolar range.
source: Analysis of isotherms from LC8 titrated into LBD-OD and the one- and two-site mutants with the one-set-of-sites (OSS) model shows enthalpically favorable interactions with Kd in the sub-micromolar to low micromolar range (Figure 5K, Table 3).
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: Both QT1 and QT3 binding give non-sigmoidal isotherms attributed to multistep binding.
source: Interestingly, both QT1 and QT3 binding give non-sigmoidal isotherms that we attribute to multistep binding.
evidence: Based on inference from ITC isotherm shapes.

claim: Two chains of the 53BP1 trimer bind to LC8, leaving the third chain available to bridge the available chain from another trimer.
source: One model that explains the data is that two chains of the trimer bind to LC8, leaving the third chain available to bridge the available chain from another trimer (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is a proposed model to explain the non-sigmoidal isotherms.

claim: Titrating QT3-OD into LC8 produces a perfectly sigmoidal isotherm, indicating that no intermediate is formed.
source: Titrating QT3-OD into LC8 produced a perfectly sigmoidal isotherm, indicating that no intermediate is formed in line with our model (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by ITC data from reverse titration.

claim: The sigmoidal isotherm observed when titrating LC8 into QT2-OD can be explained as due to the intermediate being only briefly occupied.
source: The sigmoidal isotherm observed when titrating LC8 into QT2-OD can be explained as due to the intermediate being only briefly occupied, suggesting that the bridging interaction has a stronger binding affinity similar to that of the intratrimeric LC8 binding than with the other single site mutants.
evidence: Based on inference from ITC isotherm shape.

claim: The bridging interaction of QT2-OD has a stronger binding affinity similar to that of the intratrimeric LC8 binding than with the other single site mutants.
source: The sigmoidal isotherm observed when titrating LC8 into QT2-OD can be explained as due to the intermediate being only briefly occupied, suggesting that the bridging interaction has a stronger binding affinity similar to that of the intratrimeric LC8 binding than with the other single site mutants.
evidence: Based on inference from ITC data and SBS model fitting.

claim: For the intratrimer interactions, the difference in affinity for each variant is very small (Kd between 0.3 and 0.6 µM).
source: For the intratrimer interactions, the difference in affinity for each variant is very small (Kd between 0.3 and 0.6 µM), while the difference between affinities for bridging interactions is larger (Kd between 1 and 5 µM).
evidence: Supported by ITC data analyzed with SBS model.

claim: The difference between affinities for bridging interactions is larger (Kd between 1 and 5 µM).
source: For the intratrimer interactions, the difference in affinity for each variant is very small (Kd between 0.3 and 0.6 µM), while the difference between affinities for bridging interactions is larger (Kd between 1 and 5 µM).
evidence: Supported by ITC data analyzed with SBS model.

claim: QT2-OD has the strongest affinity for the bridging interaction.
source: Additionally, the fact that QT2-OD has the strongest affinity for the bridging interaction provides a mechanistic explanation for our observation that QT2 is essential for a strongly bridged dimer-of-trimers complex.
evidence: Supported by ITC data analyzed with SBS model.

claim: All LBD-ODm with QT2 binding removed show isotherms consistent with two-step binding.
source: Additionally, all LBD-ODm with QT2 binding removed show isotherms consistent with two-step binding.
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: All interactions of two-site mutants with LC8 have affinities around 0.5 μM.
source: All interactions have affinities around 0.5 μM, but QT13-OD, the only two-site mutant not containing QT2, gives a non-sigmoidal isotherm.
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: QT13-OD gives a non-sigmoidal isotherm.
source: All interactions have affinities around 0.5 μM, but QT13-OD, the only two-site mutant not containing QT2, gives a non-sigmoidal isotherm.
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: When QT13-OD is titrated into LC8, the isotherm becomes sigmoidal.
source: Again, when we reverse the direction of titration (QT13-OD into LC8), the isotherm becomes sigmoidal (Figure 5H and I).
evidence: Supported by ITC data from reverse titration.

claim: All LBD-ODm containing QT2 have sigmoidal isotherms.
source: Since all LBD-ODm containing QT2 have sigmoidal isotherms, we attribute the non-sigmoidal isotherms to the formation of a trimeric intermediate
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: For ASCIZ, linker length contributes to both compositional and conformational heterogeneity.
source: For ASCIZ, which binds LC8 multivalently to regulate transcription, linker length contributes to both compositional (Walker et al., 2023) and conformational (Reardon et al., 2020) heterogeneity.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ITC shows sigmoidal isotherms for both linker deletion mutants.
source: In support of this model, ITC shows sigmoidal isotherms for both linker deletion mutants (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by ITC data.

claim: Mutations within the LC8 binding anchor have large impacts on binding, but the –1 position exhibits the most variability.
source: Mutations within the LC8 binding anchor have large impacts on binding, but the –1 position exhibits the most variability (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on established knowledge of LC8 binding specificity.

claim: Within 53BP1, all three QTs contain a different residue in the –1 position.
source: Within 53BP1, all three QTs contain a different residue in the –1 position (Figure 7A, bottom).
evidence: Based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: T1171I and T1171V are expected to bind LC8.
source: Two LBD-OD QT2 variants which are still expected to bind LC8 (T1171I and T1171V), and a phosphomimetic variant which is expected to greatly reduce binding for QT2 (T1171E)
evidence: Based on knowledge of LC8 binding specificity.

claim: T1171E is expected to greatly reduce binding for QT2.
source: Two LBD-OD QT2 variants which are still expected to bind LC8 (T1171I and T1171V), and a phosphomimetic variant which is expected to greatly reduce binding for QT2 (T1171E)
evidence: Based on knowledge that phosphomimetic mutations typically disrupt LC8 binding.

claim: Both T1171I and T1171V form a mixture of complexes, presumably a trimer and bridged complexes.
source: As expected, T1171E elutes completely as a trimer complex, like QT13-OD, while both T117I and T1171V form a mixture of complexes, presumably a trimer and bridged complexes.
evidence: Supported by SEC-MALS data.

claim: 53BP1 contains a minimal focus forming (MFF) region spanning residues 1220–1711.
source: 53BP1 contains a minimal focus forming (MFF) region spanning residues 1220–1711, which includes the OD, tandem tudor domain, ubiquitin-dependent recruitment domain, and nuclear localization sequence (Zgheib et al., 2009; Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work and reference to Figure 7D.

claim: The MFF region includes the OD, tandem tudor domain, ubiquitin-dependent recruitment domain, and nuclear localization sequence.
source: 53BP1 contains a minimal focus forming (MFF) region spanning residues 1220–1711, which includes the OD, tandem tudor domain, ubiquitin-dependent recruitment domain, and nuclear localization sequence (Zgheib et al., 2009; Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work and reference to Figure 7D.

claim: Mutation of only T1171 to alanine results in loss of OD-independent foci formation.
source: In fact, previous experiments have shown that mutation of only T1171 to alanine results in loss of OD-independent foci formation (Becker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Bridging of 53BP1 trimers by LC8 is an important mechanism for regulating 53BP1 oligomeric state and function.
source: It is possible that bridging of 53BP1 trimers by LC8 is an important mechanism for regulating 53BP1 oligomeric state and function, but further research is necessary to determine whether this mechanism is physiologically relevant in 53BP1 foci formation.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation requiring further research.

claim: Current data suggest that 53BP1 is a dimer which forms higher-order assemblies under conditions of DNA damage.
source: Current data suggest that 53BP1 is a dimer which forms higher-order assemblies under conditions of DNA damage (Lou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: LC8 enhances 53BP1 foci through heterogeneous bridging of 53BP1 oligomers.
source: Here, we show a novel binding mode for LC8, bridging of trimeric client subcomplexes, and propose that LC8 improves 53BP1 focus formation through heterogeneous bridging of 53BP1 subcomplexes.
evidence: This is the main conclusion proposed based on the combined data.

claim: The stability of the bridged complex is tuned by multivalency, binding specificity of the second LC8 site, and the length of the linker separating the LC8 binding domain and OD.
source: The stability of the bridged complex is tuned by multivalency, binding specificity of the second LC8 site, and the length of the linker separating the LC8 binding domain and OD.
evidence: Based on combined data from ITC, SEC-MALS, and linker deletion experiments.

claim: Only the second of the three LC8 recognition motifs is necessary for a stable bridged complex.
source: Analytical ultracentrifugation and isothermal titration calorimetry demonstrate that only the second of the three LC8 recognition motifs is necessary for a stable bridged complex.
evidence: Supported by AUC and ITC data.
